currency: title theme v3, A minor waltz, 3/4, 126 bpm, seven voices on NES 2A03 plus Konami VRC6

rate_policy.basis: Fallback of the card: 3 to 6 percent of melody notes carry a resolved dissonance, plus at most one risk 3 clash per 8 bars. MUS-DATA-STATS does not exist in this repository (checked 2026-10-21), so the band is derived from the published per theme chromatic shares already recorded in knowledge/MUSIC-STYLE-BIBLE.md.
derivation: Notes per 8 bars: the Hooktheory analyses give 0.88 to 0.89 beats per melody note in 4/4 [S51, S52, S53], which is 4.49 notes per bar and 36.0 notes per 8 bars; the waltz case is 3 beats per bar at 0.89 beats per note, which is 3.37 notes per bar and 27.0 notes per 8 bars.
Three percent of 27 to 36 notes is 0.8 to 1.1 devices and six percent is 1.6 to 2.2 devices, so the working budget is 1 or 2 devices per 8 bars, which is one per phrase.

The measured chromatic share of melody notes across four NES themes is 5, 9, 20 and 18 percent, mean 13.0 [S51, S52, S53, S56]; 3 to 6 percent is therefore 23 to 46 percent of the chromatic notes those themes actually carry, so the band is a taste budget and not a cap on everything chromatic.
At 126 bpm in 3/4 one bar is 1.43 s and 8 bars is 11.4 s, so one device per phrase lands every 11 s in the title theme, which is often enough to be heard and rare enough to stay a device.
Risk 3 devices are capped at one per 8 bars and spaced at least 4 bars apart, because a strong clash that repeats stops being a clash and starts being the style of the piece.

1.name: colour
1.meaning: An adult chromatic note a listener hears as style, not as a mistake: passing tones, neighbour tones, prepared suspensions, anticipations. Safe on any bar that the forbidden list allows.

2.name: edge
2.meaning: A deliberate oddity that a first time listener notices once, such as an appoggiatura on a strong beat, a borrowed iv, a secondary dominant, a deceptive cadence. Needs a clean resolution and at least 2 beats of quiet after it.

3.name: clash
3.meaning: A strong dissonance: b9 over a dominant, a tritone in the riff, a semitone clash between two voices, a cluster stab, a Neapolitan, a tritone substitution, the wrong note gag. Never more than one per 8 bars, never on a leitmotif end, never in the final cadence bar.

forbidden.rule: Never on the first or the last note of a leitmotif statement: K, K2, Z, P or H, in any section, including the reprise in the title theme and the transpositions in the character themes.
forbidden.check: the note index is not 0 and not the final index of any motif span tagged K, K2, Z, P or H in the score

forbidden.rule: Never in the final cadence bar of a section, of the loop, or of the cue, and never on the tonic arrival the cadence lands on.
forbidden.check: the device bar is not the last bar of any section and not the bar of a cadence arrival

forbidden.rule: Never on the first note of the loop and never in the first bar of the cue, because the listener has not yet heard the key and a clash reads as a wrong note.
forbidden.check: the bar index is at least the value of first_allowed_bar in the injector settings, which is 1 for the cue and 1 after the loop point

forbidden.rule: Never closer than 2 beats to another device, and never closer than 4 bars to a risk 3 device.
forbidden.check: the gap in beats to the previous and next device is at least 2, and the gap in bars to any risk 3 device is at least 4

forbidden.rule: Never on a note that is itself the resolution of another device, and never in the same beat as another device's resolution.
forbidden.check: the device slot is not the resolution slot of any other device

forbidden.rule: Never on the last beat before a section change, because the release happens where the harmony changes and the resolution is lost.
forbidden.check: the resolution slot lies inside the same section as the device slot

forbidden.rule: Never under a note that is held longer than 2 beats unless the score gives an earlier resolution slot, because a clash with nowhere to go is the one thing that sounds like a bug.
forbidden.check: the resolution slot exists in the written melody, not only in the harmony

forbidden.rule: Never on a bar where fewer than 2 melody notes remain after the device slot, and never in a bar whose chord is the tonic of the final cadence.
forbidden.check: the count of remaining melody notes after the device slot is at least 2

rules.name: Chromatic passing tone, rising
rules.trigger: Two melody notes on the same chord are a whole tone apart and the lower one is at least a beat long, so one semitone can be inserted between them.
recipe: Take the lower chord tone on its beat.
Insert a note one semitone below the upper chord tone on the second half of the beat or on the next eighth.
Move by semitone to the upper chord tone, which is a chord tone of the same chord or of the next chord in the bar.
Keep the inserted note at the same loudness as its neighbours and one frame of duty brighter, so it reads as a slide and not as an accent.

chord_context: any diatonic chord where the two melody notes are a whole tone apart
the same chord across the bar line

resolution.target: the upper chord tone that the semitone leads into

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1, one frame of duty change; the echo voice stays diatonic so the semitone is heard once, not twice.
rules.test: the inserted pitch class is not in the key's scale, the next note is a chord tone of the sounding chord, and the gap is one semitone
rules.example_key: A minor: A to B filled with A#, or G to A filled with G#

rules.name: Chromatic lower neighbour
rules.trigger: A melody note is held at least 2 beats and the bar has room for a dip and a return.
recipe: Keep the chord tone on its beat.
On the next weak position, step down one semitone and hold for one eighth or one beat.
Return to the same chord tone, the same octave, so the neighbour resolves to the note it left.
Change the duty one step for the neighbour only, and put the echo voice a third below and diatonic, so the semitone is not doubled.

chord_context: any chord where the melody note is the root, third or fifth
a static chord held for 2 bars

resolution.target: the same chord tone the neighbour left, same pitch class and octave

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1 with a one frame duty step; the VRC6 saw pad holds the chord tone underneath so the return is audible.
rules.test: the neighbour is one semitone below the resolving note and the resolving note equals the prepared note
rules.example_key: A minor: E to D# and back to E, or A to G# and back to A

rules.name: Appoggiatura on a strong beat, resolving down by step
rules.trigger: A phrase has a strong beat chord tone that can be approached by leap, and the next beat is available for the resolution.
recipe: On beat 1 or beat 2, enter by a leap of a third to a seventh from a chord tone of the previous beat.
Land on a note one semitone or one whole tone above the chord tone that belongs on that beat, so the strong beat carries the dissonance.
Hold one beat, or half the value of the note it replaces.
Resolve down by step to the chord tone on the next beat, at the same loudness, with no echo doubling on the dissonance.

chord_context: the tonic, subdominant or dominant chord of the section
a chord that lasts at least 2 beats

resolution.target: the chord tone a step below the appoggiatura, a member of the same chord

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1 or VRC6 pulse, with the vibrato delayed until the resolution so the dissonance is steady and the release sings.
rules.test: the strong beat note is not a chord tone, the following note is a chord tone one or two semitones below, and the duration is at most one beat
rules.example_key: A minor over Am: B held on the beat, resolving to A; or F held on the beat over Am, resolving to E

rules.name: Suspension 4 to 3
rules.trigger: The previous chord contains the note a fourth above the coming bass, so it can be prepared as a chord tone before the chord changes.
recipe: Prepare the fourth above the coming bass as a chord tone in the previous bar.
Tie or repeat that same pitch into the new chord, where it is now a dissonance against the bass.
Hold the suspension for one beat, over the bass sounding the new root.
Resolve down a semitone to the third above the bass, on the next beat.

chord_context: V resolving to i
i resolving to iv
any chord change where the fourth above the new bass was a chord tone in the old chord
section: the bar before a phrase end

resolution.target: the third above the sounding bass, a chord tone of the new chord

rules.chip: Two pulse voices, one holding the suspended note and one taking the third; the triangle plays the new root so the interval is measurable against the bass.
rules.test: the suspended pitch equals the previous chord's fourth above the new bass, and the resolution is a semitone down onto the new chord's third
rules.example_key: A minor: D suspended over an E bass, resolving to C#; or A suspended over an F bass, resolving to G#

rules.name: Suspension 7 to 6
rules.trigger: A seventh above the coming bass is available as a chord tone in the previous chord, which happens on any stepwise descending bass or a circle of fifths move.
recipe: Sound the seventh above the coming bass in the previous chord.
Carry that pitch across the chord change, where it is a seventh against the new bass and not a chord tone.
Hold it for one beat.
Resolve down a whole tone to the sixth above the bass, or down a semitone when the key is minor and the sixth is raised.

chord_context: ii to V
vi to ii
V to i in a descending bass passage

resolution.target: the sixth above the sounding bass, or the chord tone a step below the suspended note

rules.chip: Pad sawtooth holds the seventh while the lead takes the sixth; the echo channel is muted for that beat so the suspension is one interval, not two.
rules.test: the suspended pitch is the seventh above the sounding bass and the resolution is one or two semitones down onto a chord tone
rules.example_key: A minor: G suspended over an A bass resolving to F; or F suspended over a G bass resolving to E

rules.name: Suspension 9 to 8 over a dominant
rules.trigger: A dominant chord is held for at least 2 beats and the ninth above its root was a chord tone of the chord before it.
recipe: Prepare the ninth above the dominant root as a chord tone in the previous chord, for example the fifth of the tonic chord.
Hold it into the dominant, where it is a dissonant ninth above the bass.
Keep the bass on the dominant root for the whole suspension.
Resolve down a whole tone, or a semitone in a minor key with a flat ninth, to the octave above the bass, which is the dominant root.

chord_context: V or V7 held for 2 or more beats
a half cadence approached by a prepared ninth
section: the bar before a half cadence

resolution.target: the octave above the bass, which is the dominant root

rules.chip: Lead holds the ninth, pad takes the octave, triangle stays on the dominant root; no vibrato during the suspension.
rules.test: the suspended pitch is a ninth above the sounding dominant bass and the resolution is the same pitch class as that bass
rules.example_key: A minor: F held over an E7 bass, resolving to E; or B held over an E bass, resolving to E in another octave

rules.name: Accented passing tone on beat 2 of a waltz bar
rules.trigger: A 3/4 bar has a melody note on beat 1 and another on beat 3 with a whole tone between them.
recipe: Keep the beat 1 note.
Put the chromatic note that lies between beat 1 and beat 3 on beat 2 instead of the passing note of the scale, so the beat itself is the dissonance.
Hold beat 2 for its full beat, then step to the beat 3 chord tone.
Drop the bass and arpeggio one dynamic level under beat 2 so the clash is exposed and not muddy.

chord_context: any chord held for the whole bar
a bar where beat 1 and beat 3 are a whole tone apart

resolution.target: the beat 3 chord tone that the passing note leads to

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1 only; the echo voice plays the beat 1 note again, diatonic, so the accented passing note is unique in the texture.
rules.test: the beat 2 note is not a chord tone, beat 3 is a chord tone, and the interval between them is one semitone
rules.example_key: A minor over Am: A on beat 1, A# on beat 2, B on beat 3

rules.name: Escape tone
rules.trigger: A weak position sits between two chord tones and the line can afford a skip back in the opposite direction.
recipe: Approach the weak position by step from a chord tone.
Place a note outside the chord there, either chromatic or a scale note that is not in the chord.
Resolve by a leap of a third or a fourth in the opposite direction onto a chord tone of the same chord.
Keep both notes short, half a beat each, with the same duty so the shape, not the timbre, carries the oddity.

chord_context: any chord held for at least one beat
the approach chord and the resolution chord may differ

resolution.target: a chord tone of the sounding chord reached by a leap in the opposite direction

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1, with the echo a third below on the resolution only; the skip is what makes it read as an ornament rather than a wrong note.
rules.test: the escape note is approached by step, left by a leap of 3 to 5 semitones, and the landing note is a chord tone
rules.example_key: A minor over Am: A up to B, then down a third to G, or E up to F and down to D

rules.name: Anticipation of the next chord's third
rules.trigger: A bar line is one eighth away and the next chord's third is a semitone or a tone from the melody note being played.
recipe: On the last eighth of the bar, play the next chord's third early.
Hold or repeat that pitch across the bar line, where it becomes a chord tone.
Keep it one eighth long at most, at reduced loudness.
Do not double it in the echo channel until after the bar line.

chord_context: any chord change at the bar line
a phrase where the next chord is the relative major or the dominant

resolution.target: the same pitch class, now a chord tone of the next chord after the bar line

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1, one step quieter on the anticipation; the triangle changes root on the bar line, which is what makes the early note sound like a forward lean.
rules.test: the anticipated pitch equals the next chord's third and the same pitch class sounds inside that chord after the bar line
rules.example_key: A minor to C major: E played on the last eighth of the Am bar, held into the C chord

rules.name: Retardation 7 to 8
rules.trigger: A tied note sits a tone below the coming chord tone and the upward resolution is the point of the gesture.
recipe: Prepare the lower note as a chord tone of the previous chord.
Tie it across the chord change, where it is a dissonance below the chord tone it will become.
Hold for one beat.
Resolve upward by step, the one legitimate upward resolution of a tied dissonance, and mark it with a one frame volume lift so the ear catches the direction.

chord_context: V to i with the leading tone tied
any chord change where the prepared note is a tone below a new chord tone

resolution.target: the chord tone one or two semitones above the tied note

rules.chip: Lead ties the note, pad takes the resolution, no echo doubling on the dissonance beat; the VRC6 pulse duty is one step narrower on the resolution.
rules.test: the tied note is a nonchord tone against the new chord and the resolution is a step above it onto a chord tone
rules.example_key: A minor: G sharp tied over an A minor chord, resolving up to A

rules.name: Dominant seven flat nine
rules.trigger: A dominant chord lands on a strong beat and lasts at least 2 beats, and the tonic note is a semitone above its fifth.
recipe: Write the dominant seventh as root, major third, fifth and minor seventh, which is the ordinary V7.
Add the flat ninth above the root in the lead or the pad, not in both.
Hold the flat nine for one beat or until the chord changes, with the bass stationary on the root.
Resolve the flat nine down a semitone to the fifth of the tonic chord; if the lead cannot reach it, drop the pad instead and keep the lead diatonic.

chord_context: V7 in a minor key
a dominant that resolves to the tonic within 2 bars
a secondary dominant that lands on a minor chord

resolution.target: the fifth of the chord the dominant resolves to, or any chord tone a semitone below the flat nine

rules.chip: Lead holds the flat nine as a VRC6 pulse, the pad plays the seventh, the triangle plays the root; the two pulse channels are never both on the flat nine, because the mixer beats.
rules.test: the chord contains root, third, fifth, minor seventh and a note nine semitones above the root, and the flat nine falls a semitone at the resolution
rules.example_key: A minor: E7 flat 9 spelled E, G sharp, B, D, F with F resolving to E

rules.name: Tritone as a riff note
rules.trigger: A bass or stab riff repeats over a static root and there is no third in the harmony, so the tritone is the only colour.
recipe: Build the riff on the root plus the fifth, with no third, so the harmony stays open.
Alternate the root with the note a tritone above it on the eighth notes or on the offbeats.
Keep the harmonic rhythm stagnant for 2 or 4 bars, which is what makes the interval read as colour instead of a mistake.
End the riff on the root, and never put the tritone on the final note of the loop.

chord_context: a static minor tonic with no third
a dominant where the tritone is already the chord's own tension

resolution.target: the riff's own root at the end of the 2 or 4 bar figure, and a chord tone of the next chord when the harmony changes

rules.chip: Bass pulse or triangle alternating root and tritone; the VRC6 saw doubles the root only, so the tritone never gains a second voice and never becomes a cluster.
rules.test: the riff contains a note 6 semitones above the root, the chord voicing has no third, and the last note of the figure is the root
rules.example_key: E minor riff: E and A sharp alternating under an open fifth, returning to E

rules.name: Neapolitan flat two in first inversion
rules.trigger: A minor key section needs a stronger subdominant before the dominant, and the melody note on the strong beat is the flat second or can be reached by step.
recipe: Replace the subdominant or the supertonic with a major chord on the flat second, in first inversion so the bass is the fourth degree.
Hold it for one bar or for two beats.
Resolve to the dominant on the next beat or bar.
Take the flat second in the melody down a semitone to the tonic, so the alteration is heard as a colour and not as a key change.

chord_context: the bar before V in a minor key
a half cadence approach
iv or ii replaced
section: the bar before a half cadence

resolution.target: the dominant root or the tonic, a chord tone of the next chord, with the flat second falling a semitone

rules.chip: Pad sawtooth plays the triad, triangle plays the fourth degree in the bass, lead takes the flat second and resolves it by semitone; the echo voice is silent for the bar.
rules.test: the chord root is one semitone above the tonic and the chord is major with its third in the bass, and the flat second in the melody falls a semitone
rules.example_key: A minor: B flat major with D in the bass, resolving to E7

rules.name: Deceptive cadence
rules.trigger: A phrase is written to end on the tonic and the melody's leading tone resolves upward as usual, so only the bass can be diverted.
recipe: Keep the dominant on the beat before the expected tonic.
Move the bass and the chord to the sixth degree instead of the tonic, or to the flat sixth in a minor key for a darker turn.
Resolve the leading tone in the melody up to the tonic as written, so the ear hears the arrival without the bass confirming it.
Return to the dominant within 2 bars, or start the next phrase a fourth higher so the withheld tonic is paid back later.

chord_context: V to vi in a major key
V to flat VI in a minor key
the phrase end that the score marks as an authentic cadence

resolution.target: the dominant or the tonic within 2 bars, with the leading tone resolving up a semitone to the tonic in the melody

rules.chip: Pad and triangle take the substituted chord, lead keeps the leading tone; one extra frame of release on the pad so the surprise is heard as harmony, not as a cut.
rules.test: the chord after the dominant is not the tonic, and the melody's leading tone still rises to the tonic
rules.example_key: A minor: E7 to F major instead of E7 to Am, with G sharp rising to A in the melody

rules.name: Secondary dominant
rules.trigger: A diatonic chord lands on a strong beat and can be preceded by its own dominant for one beat or one bar.
recipe: Pick the target chord inside the progression, usually the subdominant, the supertonic or the dominant.
Write the dominant seventh of that target for one beat or one bar, which brings in one chromatic note, the raised third of the target.
Resolve the chromatic note by step to a chord tone of the target chord.
Do not modulate: the target must arrive on the next beat or bar and must not be tonicised for longer than a phrase.

chord_context: V7 of V
V7 of iv
V7 of ii
V7 of VI

resolution.target: the target chord on the next beat or bar, with the chromatic third resolving by step into a chord tone of it

rules.chip: Pad sawtooth plays the seventh chord, bass takes the root, lead takes the chromatic third and resolves it; the lead's duty is one step brighter for the chromatic note.
rules.test: the inserted chord is major with a minor seventh, its root is a fifth above the target root, and the target chord follows inside the allowed window
rules.example_key: A minor: B7 to E7, or A7 to Dm, or G7 to C

rules.name: Borrowed minor four from the parallel minor
rules.trigger: A major key section reaches the subdominant, which is the moment a borrowed minor subdominant can darken the phrase.
recipe: Replace the major subdominant with the minor subdominant from the parallel minor, which lowers the third by a semitone.
Hold it for one bar or for two beats.
Resolve the lowered sixth in the melody down to the fifth of the tonic, or keep it in the pad and let the lead stay diatonic.
Return to the diatonic key on the next chord so the borrowing stays brief.

chord_context: IV to iv in a major key
the bar before the tonic or the dominant

resolution.target: the fifth of the tonic, or any chord tone of the next chord that the lowered sixth can reach by step

rules.chip: Pad sawtooth holds the minor subdominant; the lead's lowered sixth is a VRC6 pulse so it stands out from the 2A03 texture; bass stays on the fourth degree.
rules.test: the chord is minor on the fourth degree of a major key, and the lowered sixth resolves down by step
rules.example_key: C major: F minor instead of F major, with A flat falling to G

rules.name: Flat six to five approach
rules.trigger: A minor key phrase can walk down the bass from the flat sixth to the fifth before the dominant.
recipe: Write the flat sixth chord for one beat or one bar, borrowed from the parallel minor of the relative major or drawn from harmonic minor.
Move the bass down a semitone, or the melody down a semitone, to the fifth degree.
Land on the dominant, or on the tonic six four, on the next beat.
Keep the rest of the texture diatonic so only one note is chromatically altered.

chord_context: flat VI to V in a minor key
the approach to a half cadence

resolution.target: the dominant root, reached by a falling semitone from the flat sixth

rules.chip: Pad and triangle move together on the semitone; the noise channel is silent for the approach beat, which makes the bass motion audible.
rules.test: the chord root is a minor sixth above the tonic, the next chord is the dominant, and the bass falls exactly one semitone
rules.example_key: A minor: F major to E7, with F falling to E in the bass

rules.name: Cross voice minor second between echo and lead
rules.trigger: The echo channel is echoing the lead with a delay, and the lead moves to a note a semitone from the echo's held pitch.
recipe: Let the echo channel hold the lead's previous note.
Move the lead to a note one semitone above or below the echo's held pitch, on a weak or a strong position the forbidden list allows.
Hold the clash for exactly one beat, or for as long as the echo's delay makes it unavoidable.
Resolve the lead by a semitone, or release the echo, so the two voices meet on a unison or a chord tone on the next beat.

chord_context: a chord where the semitone is a flat ninth or a major seventh against the echo's note
any harmony, since the clash is horizontal

resolution.target: a unison with the echo, or a chord tone one semitone away from the clash, reached by the lead or by the echo's release

rules.chip: Lead on pulse 1, echo on pulse 2 at one half volume, so the semitone is a beating shimmer; never put the clash between the two VRC6 pulses, which are too close in timbre and turn to mud.
rules.test: the two voices' pitches differ by one semitone, the clash lasts at most one beat, and the next event in either voice is a unison or a chord tone
rules.example_key: A minor: lead on E while the echo holds F, then the lead falls to E flat or the echo releases to E

rules.name: Augmented chord on a pickup
rules.trigger: A phrase or a section begins on a downbeat and the bar before it has an eighth or a beat free.
recipe: On the pickup, play an augmented triad built on the root a semitone below the coming chord's root, or on the same root with a raised fifth.
Hold it for one eighth or one beat only.
Resolve at the downbeat onto the coming chord, with the raised fifth rising a semitone to the new root or the new third.
Keep the bass out of the pickup, so the augmented chord is a stab and not a harmony.

chord_context: the beat before a section downbeat
the beat before a secondary dominant
the beat before a deceptive resolution

resolution.target: a chord tone of the chord at the following downbeat, with the raised fifth rising a semitone

rules.chip: Both pulse channels plus one VRC6 pulse for the third note of the triad, four frames long, one frame of release; the triangle rests.
rules.test: the three pitches form a major third and an augmented fifth, the stab lasts at most one beat, and the raised fifth rises a semitone at the downbeat
rules.example_key: A minor: G augmented as the pickup into an Am downbeat, with D sharp rising to E

rules.name: Wrong note then resolve gag
rules.trigger: A cue needs one moment of humour or panic, once, and the phrase has a note the listener already expects.
recipe: On a weak position, play a note a semitone away from the expected note, or a tritone away from the bass.
Hold it for one eighth at most, then correct it to the expected note within one beat.
Use it once per cue, never in the same 16 bars, and never in the title theme's first statement of K.
Make the correction louder than the mistake, so the ear reads the first note as a slip and the second as the truth.

chord_context: any chord, since the gag is horizontal
the second bar of a phrase, never the first

resolution.target: the note the listener expected, a chord tone of the sounding chord, one or two semitones away

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1 only, with the echo muted on the gag and the correction, so the joke is dry; a one frame duty change marks the correction.
rules.test: exactly one out of key note per cue, corrected within one beat to a chord tone, and the cue contains no second gag
rules.example_key: A minor over Am: D sharp on the offbeat, corrected to E on the next eighth

rules.name: Pedal tone against changing chords
rules.trigger: A section holds its root for 2 bars or the dominant for 2 bars while the chords above move.
recipe: Choose the tonic or the dominant as the pedal.
Hold it in the triangle or in a low pulse for 2 to 4 bars, repeated on every beat or held as one long note.
Let the chords above change normally, so the pedal becomes a nonchord tone for one or two chords and then a chord tone again.
End the pedal on a bar where it is a chord tone, and never release it on a dissonance.

chord_context: a section that leaves the pedal's chord and returns to it
a dominant pedal before the loop point
section: the last 2 bars before the loop point

resolution.target: a bar where the pedal pitch is a chord tone of the sounding chord, at the end of the pedal

rules.chip: Triangle holds the pedal, because it has no volume envelope to decay; the two chords above it go in the pulse channels and the VRC6 saw, so the pedal is a floor and not a voice.
rules.test: the pedal pitch is constant across the span, at least one chord in the span does not contain it, and the last bar of the span does
rules.example_key: A minor: A held in the triangle while the chords go Am, F, E7, Am

rules.name: Cluster stab
rules.trigger: A downbeat or a section start needs a hit rather than a chord, and the noise channel can carry the attack.
recipe: Choose a chord tone and add the note a semitone or a whole tone above it in a second voice.
Play both together for one to four frames, staccato, with a sharp release.
Put the same figure an octave lower in the bass if the stab needs weight, but never add a third pitch in the low register.
Resolve by silence: the next event in that voice is a chord tone, at least an eighth later.

chord_context: the tonic or the flat six at a section start
the chord under a boss entrance
section: the first bar of the trio
the loop point if the last bar allows it

resolution.target: silence, then a chord tone at the next event in the same voice, at least an eighth note later

rules.chip: Pulse 1 and pulse 2 a semitone or a tone apart, four frames, maximum volume, immediate silence; add one frame of noise volume 4 for the transient, not more.
rules.test: two voices sound pitches a semitone or a tone apart for at most four frames, and the next event in those voices is a chord tone
rules.example_key: A minor: A and B flat together on a downbeat, four frames, then silence

rules.name: Secondary leading tone chord
rules.trigger: A chord on a strong beat can be approached from a semitone below in the bass.
recipe: Write the diminished seventh or the diminished triad on the leading tone of the target chord.
Put its root, a semitone below the target root, in the bass.
Hold it for one beat.
Resolve the bass up a semitone into the target root, and resolve the diminished seventh's own seventh down a semitone.

chord_context: vii dim 7 of V
vii dim 7 of iv
vii dim 7 of the tonic in a deceptive move

resolution.target: the target chord's root, reached by the bass rising one semitone; the chordal seventh falls one semitone

rules.chip: Pad sawtooth plays the diminished seventh, bass takes the semitone approach; the echo channel doubles the resolution, never the approach.
rules.test: the chord is diminished, built on a root one semitone below the following chord's root, and the bass rises exactly one semitone
rules.example_key: A minor: D sharp diminished seventh resolving to E7, or G sharp diminished seventh resolving to Am

rules.name: Tritone substitution at a cadence approach
rules.trigger: A dominant is approaching the tonic and the bass can fall a semitone instead of rising a fourth.
recipe: Replace the dominant seventh with the dominant seventh whose root is a tritone away, which shares the same tritone between third and seventh.
Keep the two tritone notes in the same voices, so the resolution is unchanged.
Put the substituted root in the bass for one bar or two beats.
Resolve the bass down a semitone to the tonic, and resolve the tritone as written.

chord_context: the bar before the tonic
a ii to V cadence where the V is replaced
section: the bar before the final loop cadence but not the cadence bar itself

resolution.target: the tonic, with the bass falling one semitone and the tritone resolving inward or outward as written

rules.chip: Pad plays the substitute seventh, triangle plays its root, the lead keeps the tritone note it already had so the swap is heard only in the bass.
rules.test: the substituted root is 6 semitones from the replaced dominant root, the tritone pitch classes are identical, and the bass falls one semitone to the tonic
rules.example_key: A minor: B flat 7 instead of E7, with B flat falling to A

rules.name: Suspension chain
rules.trigger: The bass descends stepwise for 3 or 4 bars and each chord change can carry a prepared dissonance.
recipe: Prepare each suspension as a chord tone of the chord before it.
Tie it across each bar line so every chord change begins with a dissonance on beat 1.
Resolve each one down by step on beat 2 or beat 3, then reprepare the next.
Keep two voices at most, so the chain is a two part texture and not a thicket.

chord_context: a descending bass of a fourth or more
a circle of fifths passage

resolution.target: the chord tone a step below the suspended note, in each bar of the chain

rules.chip: Two pulse voices in fourth species fashion; the pad is silent during the chain so the two lines are clean, and the triangle carries the descending bass.
rules.test: each bar of the chain begins with a nonchord tone that is a chord tone of the previous bar, and each resolves down by step within one beat
rules.example_key: A minor descending bass A, G, F, E with suspensions resolving on beat 2 of each bar

rules.name: Changing tones around a chord tone
rules.trigger: A melody note is repeated or held and the bar has room for a two note ornament that leaves the harmony and returns.
recipe: Start on a chord tone.
Step to a note outside the chord, then leap to a second note outside the chord, usually on the other side of the chord tone.
Return by step to the chord tone, or to another chord tone of the same chord.
Keep the whole figure inside one beat, with the same duty on both outside notes so it reads as one gesture.

chord_context: a chord held for a whole bar or more
a tonic or dominant chord that can absorb two nonchord tones

resolution.target: a chord tone of the sounding chord, reached by step from the second nonchord tone

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1 only, both nonchord tones on the same duty; the echo holds the chord tone underneath so the return is unambiguous.
rules.test: two successive nonchord tones followed by a step onto a chord tone, all inside one beat
rules.example_key: A minor over Am: A up to B, down to G, back up to A

rules.name: Chromatic bass descent under a held melody
rules.trigger: A melody note is held for 2 bars and the bass can walk down by semitones beneath it.
recipe: Choose a bass line that descends by semitones for 2 to 4 beats, from a chord tone to a chord tone.
Hold the melody constant above it, so each bass note turns the held pitch into a different interval.
Let the chords above change only on the beats where the bass lands on a chord tone.
End the descent on the fifth or the root of the next chord.

chord_context: a chord held for at least 2 bars
a tonic or subdominant chord that can sit while the bass walks

resolution.target: a chord tone of the next chord, with the bass arriving from a semitone below or above

rules.chip: Triangle walks the semitones, because it has no envelope decay; the pad holds the chord, and the noise channel is off so the walk is exposed.
rules.test: each bass step in the descent is one semitone, the melody pitch does not change during the descent, and the last bass note is a chord tone of the next chord
rules.example_key: A minor: bass A, G sharp, G, F sharp under a held C

rules.name: Major seventh held over the tonic, resolving down
rules.trigger: A tonic chord is held at the end of a phrase and the leading tone can be sustained above it.
recipe: Hold the tonic chord with the major seventh above the root, so the chord sounds like a major seventh for one beat or one bar.
Keep the seventh in the lead or the pad, never both.
Resolve the seventh down a semitone to the fifth of the chord, or up a semitone to the tonic if the line is rising.
Never end a phrase on the unresolved seventh, because a tonic major seventh has no dominant function.

chord_context: the tonic triad held for at least 2 beats
a tonic chord in a major key or a Picardy third in a minor key

resolution.target: the fifth of the tonic, a semitone below the seventh, or the tonic a semitone above

rules.chip: Pad holds the triad, lead holds the seventh at reduced volume; the seventh must be a VRC6 pulse so it does not fight the 2A03 lead's own fifth.
rules.test: the sounding interval includes a major seventh above the root and the next melody event falls a semitone onto a chord tone
rules.example_key: A minor with a Picardy third: A, C sharp, E with G sharp above, resolving to E

rules.name: Blue third slide
rules.trigger: A major chord is held and the melody reaches for the minor third before settling on the major third.
recipe: Play the minor third of the chord on a weak position.
Hold it for an eighth or half a beat, at the same loudness as the major third that follows.
Slide up a semitone to the major third on the next eighth.
Do it only over a major chord or a power chord with a major third implied; never over a minor chord, where the minor third is already the chord tone.

chord_context: a major tonic, subdominant or dominant chord
a power chord with no third

resolution.target: the major third of the sounding chord, one semitone above the blue note

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1 with the same duty for both notes, so the slide is a pitch gesture; the echo stays on the major third to anchor the resolution.
rules.test: the first note is a minor third above the chord root, the second is the major third, and the interval is one semitone
rules.example_key: C major: E flat sliding up to E

rules.name: Tritone leap answered by step
rules.trigger: A melody can afford one wide, sour leap in a bar and the bar has a step left to answer it.
recipe: Leap a tritone from a chord tone on a weak or a strong position, exactly one beat before the bar's last note.
Answer the leap by step in the opposite direction on the next note, onto a chord tone.
Keep both notes short, one eighth or one quarter, and change the duty on the leap so the interval is marked.
Use it at most once per 16 bars, never on a leitmotif statement and never in a cadence bar.

chord_context: a dominant or diminished chord where the tritone is native
a tonic chord in a comic or sinister cue

resolution.target: a chord tone one or two semitones from the tritone note, reached by a step in the opposite direction to the leap

rules.chip: Lead pulse 1, one duty step brighter on the leap, and the echo answers on the resolution only, so the leap is a single sour event.
rules.test: one melodic leap of 6 semitones, followed within one beat by a step onto a chord tone in the opposite direction
rules.example_key: A minor over E7: leap from E up to A sharp, then step down to A

S68.title: Wikipedia, Nonchord tone
S68.supports: Definitions of passing tone, neighbour tone, escape tone, anticipation, suspension (4 to 3, 7 to 6, 9 to 8), retardation, appoggiatura, changing tones, pedal point and chromatic nonharmonic tones; the statement that nonharmonic tones usually form dissonant seconds, fourths or sevenths and resolve to a chord tone; the Fux 1725 quotation urging suspensions; the note that chromatic appoggiaturas and passing tones increased in the Romantic period

S69.title: Wikipedia, Pedal point
S69.supports: A pedal point as a sustained tone, usually in the bass, against at least one foreign harmony; it begins as a chord tone, becomes a nonchord tone, and is a chord tone again when the harmony resolves; usually on the tonic or the dominant; the thrash metal muted low string as a pedal

S70.title: Wikipedia, Neapolitan chord
S70.supports: The Neapolitan as a major chord on the lowered second, most often in first inversion as the Neapolitan sixth, functioning as a subdominant substitute that prepares the dominant, and far more common in minor keys

S71.title: Wikipedia, Secondary chord
S71.supports: Secondary dominants as a major triad or dominant seventh built to resolve to a scale degree other than the tonic; V of V as the most common; the purpose being to emphasise a chord inside the diatonic progression; a tonicisation longer than a phrase counts as a modulation

S72.title: Wikipedia, Borrowed chord
S72.supports: Mode mixture as chords borrowed from the parallel key; in major the most common borrowings lower the sixth (iv, ii half diminished, flat VI); flat III and flat VII come from the parallel minor or Mixolydian; borrowed chords are brief enough that the tonic is not lost

S73.title: Wikipedia, Tone cluster
S73.supports: A tone cluster as a chord of at least three adjacent tones, prototypically semitone separated; in most Western music clusters are heard as dissonant

S74.title: Wikipedia, Altered chord
S74.supports: Alterations on dominant chords of flat five, sharp five, flat nine and sharp nine, and the statement that using one in a resolving dominant greatly increases the bite of the chord and the power of the resolution; altered notes used as leading tones to their diatonic neighbours

S75.title: Wikipedia, Tritone
S75.supports: The tritone as six semitones, a harmonic and melodic dissonance in functional harmony, and the interval whose notes push toward resolution in dominant and diminished chords; also the note that a tritone against the keynote can be used to avoid tonality

S76.title: Wikipedia, Augmented triad
S76.supports: The augmented triad as a major third plus an augmented fifth; H.R. Palmer on its resolution, where the fifth rises a minor second and the third either rises a minor second or stays; the augmented chord on V as a substitute dominant; examples in popular song introductions

S77.title: Wikipedia, Black Sabbath (song)
S77.supports: The main riff as a G5 power chord followed by an octave into a tritone away from the root, described as highlighting the dissonant dark sound of the tritone against a stagnant harmonic rhythm, and as one of the earliest metal uses of the interval
